thread.title: Netflix Shares Hit 52-Week High as Obama Rumors Fly

author: Jon Swartz
title: Netflix Shares Hit 52-Week High as Obama Rumors Fly
text:
Shares of Netflix (NFLX) hit an all-time high today, and the milestone comes on reports that former President Barack Obama and First Lady Michelle Obama are in advanced talks with the streaming service on content deals.
Illustration: Getty Images Netflix's stock climbed 3% in mid-morning trading, to $326.61. For the year, they're up nearly 69%.
The New York Times said both Obamas are discussing several possibilities , including the former president moderating conversations on topics such as immigration, health care and climate change, and the First Lady producing shows on nutrition and fitness for children.
A deal with Netflix is no slam dunk, however. The same report says Apple (AAPL) and Amazon (AMZN) have also expressed interest in talking with the Obamas about content deals on their own streaming services. (President Obama recently was the first guest on David Letterman’s Netflix original talk show, My Next Guest Needs No Introduction . Last year, Michelle Obama appeared on stage with Apple Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook and executive Lisa Jackson to discuss climate change and education at Apple's WWDC conference in San Jose, Calif.)
No one would fault Apple and Amazon for borrowing from Netflix's winning playbook, which has paid off handsomely in worldwide streaming subscriptions (118 million at last count), a recent Academy Award win for the documentary Icarus, and a surging stock, even as it plans to spend $12 billion on content.
Netflix appears to know what it's doing with that cash, explains Bernstein analyst Todd Juenger , who raised his price target on Netflix to $340 in a report today. He offered several "proof points," among them the urban crime fantasy Bright. Juenger says Netflix has "a huge advantage because members are pre-disposed to think they will ‘like' Netflix content, which usually becomes a self-fulfilling prophecy." He also nodded to the recent hiring of Ryan Murphy , an award-winning producer, director and writer, to what is believed to be the biggest TV pact ever: up to $300 million over five years . Netflix poached Murphy from 21st Century Fox (FOXA).
The Obama deal, if it happens, would just be another feather in Netflix's cap. Daniel Ives , head of technology research at GBH Insights , summed up the possibility of an Obama deal another as "major win" for Netflix. He maintains a Highly Attractive rating and price target of $375 on the stock.
